Mega Bloks Barbie Fab Mansion 200+ pieces? Well, maybe if you count each sticker on the page of stickers you can use to "customize" the house. This "mansion" contains five rooms -- bathroom bedroom, kitchen, entry hall, and living room -- along with a rooftop deck. It houses two dolls -- each about 2 inches tall -- along with a little white dog and a pink teddy bear. The dolls have assorted, interchangeable accessories -- hair bows, purses, skirts, for fun mixing and matching. But these pieces are tiny!! Most of the pieces are about the size of Barbie shoes -- so I have fear of a little plastic blow dryer and little mixing spoon and little lamp shade being sucked up into the vacuum cleaner. I think the pieces are too small for kids under 8 or so, so I'm not quite sure who the target audience is for this. My 11 year old, who has become interested in Barbies again after a several-year hiatus, wasn't too interested in this. But I thought it was fun to play with.

It's kind of fun to play with -- a nice mixture of Legos and dolls. It is not nearly as complicated as other Lego projects we've worked on. The other good thing about this is you can mix and match with other sets -- there's always more to buy to make this mansion even bigger and better. This might be fun for a few hours of play join a snowy afternoon.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Barbie Fab Mansion

text_fidelity_a:
Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set The board is a very nice, stained wood. It measures 15.75" by 15.75" (including the handles) wide by 1" deep when open or 2" when folded. It folds in half, with the recessed backgammon side holding the game pieces during storage. Two pairs of magnets hold the board closed when folded. The magnets have been effective at holding the set closed without being difficult to open when desired. The top board is 8 by 8 squares across. The wood checkers are just under 1" across and have a slight protrusion on the bottom to keep them in place when a piece is crowned. There are 15 pieces each of brown and white, and these pieces are also used for backgammon. The wood chess pieces are common, simple chess shapes and have a felt bottom. The pawns are 1 3/8" tall and the king is 3" tall. The set also includes two wooden cups, two pairs of dice, and a doubling cube for backgammon. The included game instructions are brief and not really enough to learn to play the games, but it's easy enough to find this information online. From the box: "Solid wood travel set accented with walnut, maple, and mahogany playing surfaces" as well as the California Prop 65 warning with "Wash hands after use."

There are some 1 star reviews for this set, and I have a hard time believing it's for the same set. The set I got has lovely workmanship and everything looks sturdy and well-made. The handle is plenty wide (4.25" across and 1" high) and is sanded smooth as well as finished with a stain. There is no obvious glue.
text_fidelity_b: Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set

Hot Wheels Star Wars Carships Death Star Revolution Race Track Set The box says this toy is for 5 and up. It's one of those toys that will have appeal to a great variety of ages. I could easily see any fan of Star Wars having fun playing with this thing, no matter what age, even teens and adults. I've enjoyed it myself. IF my children grow tired of it, I think I'll just claim it for my own.

The great thing about this toy is that it looks cool, too. It makes a great display toy. I prefer having toys hidden when not in use, but this one even looks great on a dresser(or something similar).

You do have to assemble it, but it didn't take me long. I gave an inward sigh of impatience when I dumped all the pieces out of the box, but it really wasn't that bad. It only took a few minutes to get it all together. Stickers have to be applied, too. Apply them carefully, because they're difficult to move without tearing.

It's loud! Conversation of any kind isn't the best idea while it's on, unless you're willing to yell to be heard. It takes 4 D batteries, and those are NOT included. We don't typically keep D batteries around, so we bought some before opening the package.

It has a place to hold up to 6 cars when not in use. It takes some practice to get the car to crash into the middle, so it's not something that will happen automatically for most.

Overall, this is a really cool toy. All my children have enjoyed it, and I have, too.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Star Wars Carships Death Star Revolution Race Track Set

Fisher-Price Imaginext Mega T-Rex My little boy is almost 3, and he loves this toy! My husband and I have even had fun with it, but probably just because our son gets so excited when the little missiles shoot up in the air. That would probably be the only warning I would have with it. For a toy, the missiles can go a good little distance, and could possible poke someone in the eye. The chances are most likely low, but it could happen.

The only thing that I somewhat didn't like is there's no directions. We just had to figure out on our own and by looking at picture on the box where the extras attached. It didn't take forever or anything, but it was annoying trying to guess at where the pieces went. That is a very minor issue, though!

The dinosaur doesn't really do a whole lot, but I think it's great for creative play. You have to hold the button down for it to roar, and as soon as you let go, it stops. As a parent, I actually really like that feature. I hate when you mash a button and have to listen to noise for several minutes. As I mentioned earlier, there are two missiles that you can launch into the air. There's also a little man that rides on the dinosaur's back. He sits in a compartment. The little flap that keeps him in this compartment comes off really easily and that annoyed my son, but it goes back on easily, too.

We like this toy so much for my son that we're planning on adding to our collection from the same line of toys this Christmas.

Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Dinosaur Toy for Boys and Girls, Red Tyrannosaurus Rex with Chomping Hinged Jaw, Ages 4+ The Schleich T-Rex is nicely done. however, it's not as detailed as the Papo brand T-Rex. When I first got this I thought it was as good as the Papo, until I started comparing the two more closely. Like the Papo brand, the jaw is articulated so it can be opened or closed. The Schleich is well made and better than many toy dinosaurs out there, but when compared side-by-side you can really see the difference between the two. The arms aren't as well done and wrinkles in the skin don't seem as real as they do with the Papo. Also, I realize we probably have no way of knowing the actual color of the dinosaurs but the red on this one makes it seem a little bit cartoonish.

This dinosaur will be great for kids that play with them regularly. They will love how realistic they look. However, if you're a collector and just want these for display, I'd suggest the Papo brand instead.

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn I've bought some of the Alex Toys for the children in our family, but this is the first Alex Junior Toy we've owned. Alex Toys are known for their sturdiness, well made enough to pass on to future generations, wonderful educational and imagination values and gorgeous vivid colors. This beautiful barn is no exception with it's sturdiness, educational value and vivid bright colors.

This barn is very sturdy, weighing over 10 pounds and made of both very smooth wood and wood products. You can easily see this lasting for future generations of babies to learn with. There are 6 sides of the barn for learning and play. The 2 sides of the roof are beautifully colored with numbers and corresponding food items- such as the number 8, shows eight ears of corn. One side of the barn has 3 barn doors that when opened, baby can see the animals living inside. The other side of the barn, has a windmill, cloud and sun that, being gears, all turn each other when moved.

The large back of the barn has a moveable tractor, cow and rooster. Baby can move these inside the tracks, so nothing comes loose. The front of the barn includes the most wonderful spinning wood blocks of the alphabet with accompanying pictures. There is a darling owl for the letter O, a cute donkey for the letter D and all the pictures that accompany the letters of the alphabet are not only adorable, but beautifully colored. We have twins in our family and this barn being 6 sided allows them to play on different sides at the same time.

I remember wood alphabet blocks being passed down from one generation to another in our family, but this gorgeous barn will replace that tradition. This barn makes it easy and fun for baby to learn both the alphabet and their numbers at the same time. Our babies love the vivid colors and they love learning that 2 means counting 2 items and that the sound of the letter J sounds like Jam. This is a beautiful barn that your baby will love learning their ABC's and 123's with. It's 5 Star Learning Fun that will last many generations to come.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn

ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay This is a really fun "spooky" game for kids. It's not really that "spooky", but it does require that you play in the dark, which can be a bit difficult for the very young, but fortunately the large hiding place pieces and the very cute shadowlings got our daughter to play the game willingly.

This is a hide-and-seek style of game in which one player moves a real, working lantern around the board trying to illuminate the shadowlings. It uses the old fashioned "roll and move" mechanic, but fortunately, the game does a good job of ensuring that you can usually get where you need to go. This is the role best suited to younger children.

Other children, or parents, will play as the Shadowlings. The lantern player closes their eyes, while the other players move shadowlings that are not illuminated in an attempt to hide them from the lantern-holding player. This role is better for adults because the rules are a little vague and open to interpretation in this area. Technically, you are allowed to move anywhere, so long as you are not illuminated and I think that's difficult for children to judge fairly (even the adults had an argument about it).

Overall, this is a good kids game, and adults can have some fun too. I wish the rules were a little clearer on how to lay out terrain, what "illuminated' really means, and so forth, but then again, too much of that would make the manual unreadable. Maybe some picture examples would have been ideal. As it is, your children will need some experience with this game with parents before you can let them play alone, but it is clever and, unlike many children's games, it's good for parents too.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Shadows in the Forest Play in the Dark Board Game for Kids and Families Age 8 and Up - Fun and Easy to Learn with Innovative and Unique Gameplay

LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist Electronic Scrabble Twist is a great idea and it more like an electronic version of Boggle in which players can make as many three, four, or five letter words as possible from a random group of letters before time runs out. Simply press the buttons on the unit to spell the words and “twist” to save the word - the bigger the word, the more points you receive for that word. Unfortunately, I love the idea more than the execution. There are both good and bad features of the game, which I’ve summarized below.

Good:
• Games are quick and rules are basic
• The game can be played by anywhere from 1 to 8 players, depending on the game mode
• There are different games that can be played and different levels of difficulty with varying lengths of the time players are given to find words
• The game quickly shuts off automatically if not in use
• The letters will automatically display in the right direction even if the unit is turned, which is good for the party mode in which the unit is passed and also means it works well for both left and right handed players
• The Turbo mode, for head-to-head play between two or more players is fun
• The sound can be turned off for quieter play

Not So Good:

• The worst part of the game is that the letters are hard to read and is a strain on your eyes after playing for a while. People in my family of all age groups said the same thing.
• Three AA batteries are required, but they’re not included
• The instructions on using the game unit aren’t clear (I was able to figure out how to use it by playing the game a few times.)
• The solo mode tracks high scores, but not by name. It doesn’t feel like you’re working toward anything since you can’t really compare scores from game to game since it depends on the letters you had for each game.
• When the sound is on, it’s loud, even at the lowest level. Different sounds do alert you that you’ve played a valid word. A second sound plays if the word you’ve played is invalid or a duplicate. Sounds also let you know if time is about to run out, but I found that this distracted me from finding my final words
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist

Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up In the 50's and 60's Board Games and Cards were very popular. I remember playing Yahtzee in the 60's mainly with older family than with friends. The older people in the 50's and 60's loved cards- my Mother's friends had Bridge Clubs and the men loved their Poker Nights. I always felt Yahtzee was a combination of a board type game using dice combined with the skill of cards.

The object of Yahtzee is to get the most points by figuring out the points the dice will give you with 3 of a kind, large straight, full house, aces and other card type combinations. You get three chances to roll the most points you can figure out. You really had to figure out which dice would get you more points on the upper section or the lower section of your score card to score high. They even included chips in the game, as you could get a chip for every 100 points you score.

When you roll the 5 dice all the same number, that was Yahtzee. It's nice to see Classic games coming around again to enjoy. For anyone who likes the strategy of playing cards, only with rolling 5 dice, Yahtzee brings that and more to this classic 50's game of both skill and chance.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition I very much liked the original edition of Werewords (essentially the same game as Insider), and this is the same game, but there's more of it.

Werewords is a lot like "20 questions". Players ask yes/no questions in an attempt to identify a word that could be anything from "spatula" to "Mjollnir". One player is a werewolf, who knows the word already, and is attempting to guide the players with their questioning closer to the actual word without them figuring out that they know the word already. They win if players can identify the word, but do not know which among them is the werewolf. If they do identify the werewolf, then the werewolf can also identify the "seer" player (another with information about the word).

The deluxe edition contains a few additional roles for players. If you already have the other version of this game, I don't think you need to own this version unless you're a completionist. If you don't own any versions of this game, I think it's quite good.

My concern remains the same as before - the app for this game is good, and it doesn't appear to be going anywhere, but if you don't want to run an app while playing this game, then I totally understand, and this game will not be for you at all. I think the app does a good job of balancing the words against one another, creating the ability to discern easy from very difficult words, but the same effect could have been accomplished with cards. I would prefer the cards as well, but the app has the advantage of saving shelf space and also having a larger directory of words. In the end, it's a toss up, but if you don't mind the app, then this is the best possible edition of the game to get.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Werewords Deluxe Edition

text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

Lift a yellow door off of Thomas's back and you'll find a number of large Mega blocks in multiple colors -- purple, red, orange, green, yellow, and blue -- stored inside, along with a sheet of stickers for decorating the blocks with numbers and train pictures.  The blocks can be used to build structures on top of Thomas or separately, and they can be used with other Mega blocks. text_fidelity_a:
Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set Our kids, ages 3-10, went crazy seeing this Angry Birds- Sling And Smash Track Set. The set couldn't be more easy to set up. It comes with a spring loaded sling shot with a slide to propel Red, the Angry Bird into destroying Pig City. The city has 2 buildings that sit on 4 ladders. You can make the city any way you want and stand the green pig anywhere. There are stickers included to make the buildings look more real. Once set up, all you do, is pull back the spring and Red, who has a wheel base, either flies or rolls into the pig city, knocking it down along with the green pig. The play is simple, but after a while, our kids starting begging for paper towel cardboard tubes, toilet paper tubes, Tupperware, plastic cups, building blocks, anything light and stackable to build pig city taller, wider, bigger and more fun.

They began cutting windows into the paper towel tubes, so the green pig could watch the bird coming. Then they began decorating the tubes, along with our small Ziploc and Tupperware containers. Soon, there was a pig city big enough to play targeting the city all day. I should have known what was coming next. I soon heard begging, that they desperately need more pigs for the city and more birds to attack. So, I found Amazon has extra figures- Angry Birds Movie Mini Figure Multi Pack Set A and a Set B. Each Set includes both birds and pigs- 7 total figures. They are not expensive- around $13.00 for each 7 figure set. So, I bought both sets, and the figures are very cute, making them worth buying just for their cuteness alone. Now, what was a simple fun Red Angry Bird attacking a lone Green Pig in a little 2 building Pig City has turned into 14 more Angry Birds and Pigs living in a Pig City Block designed from cardboard tubes, small Tupperware containers, blocks and wood scraps all designed from our children's imaginations. This simple little Set is a Big 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: Angry Birds - Sling and Smash Track Set

HEXBUG nano Robotic Cat - Interactive Automated Toy, Stimulate Hunting Instinct of Your Feline and Create Exercising Opportunities - Ships Assorted When they hear it switch on, they will all jump down from the bed upstairs and come running downstairs to play with it. The downside is they will chase it under the stove, behind a cabinet, under the couch, and generally places that are a pain to retrieve it from. That has limited how often we get it out for them to play with it, but when we do, they are obsessed. Lots of reviews say the battery life is horrible, so I got the extra batteries, but we are still on the original. Granted, we don't leave it out all day for them (it isn't a loud toy, but when it goes underneath something and starts vibrating against it, that can be very loud).

Full disclosure: on the second or third day of having this toy, one of our cats bit down on it, causing one of the legs to come off. The legs are tiny and not a choking or digestive concern, but this made it unbalanced, causing it to go in tiny circles and not move in straight lines anymore. I was able to find Hexbugs made for kids in the toy section of a local big box store, but without the fluffy tail. This makes the bug even more likely to go underneath things, so stick with the fluffy tailed version!

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game "Monopoly Empire" is like a simplified version of the traditional game of Monopoly. The colors and layout of the board are very similar to the traditional game, but each has a famous logo, such as Hasbro or EA Sports, instead of street names. The object of the game is to add tiles with various brands to your Times Square type "billboard tower" before the other players. The more brands you add to your billboard, the more money you get when passing Go, which allows you to buy more brands. The game tokens are representative of the brands in the game, such as a bottle of Coca-Cola and an Xbox controller. The board is a bit smaller than the traditional board, because it doesn't have railroads.

The game is easy to learn, in part because of an excellent, full-color instruction guide that includes a very clear diagram of how to set up the board. The way the items are priced make it easy to pay for purchased tiles. Although the game is lacking the excitement and strategy of trading properties and building houses as in the original version of Monopoly, it is good for a quick game. It would be easy for kids to learn and play. The game is most fun when it's a close race between the players to complete their towers. If one player takes a large, early lead, it's hard for the other person to come from behind.

Note: The logoed tiles have various sizes, which is part of the game. However, the sometimes the positioning of the stickers with the logo make it confusing to put them into the tower correctly.

All in all, this is a good game that is easy to play and goes by quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, Silly Wheelie Mickey When I first saw this in the flesh, I must say I was impressed (and a little jealous).  It's bigger, heavier (in a good way), and more robust than what I imagined, and it seems really well built.  The toy is ready to go (batteries included) and seems built for real world use.  It works best on hard floors (laminate and wood especially), and the little rubber tracks in the rear wheel (which doesn't rotate as wheels do) do a good job of moving the bike, popping wheelies, and avoiding picking up too much of the hair and debris my St Bernard leaves in his wake.  Speaking of which, the big dog and cats love it too.  The toy moves better than you'd think, and it's every bit as durable as you'd like.  It does get stuck along the wall or fall over, but it keeps going.  Carpet doesn't work nearly as well as harder surfaces.  I wouldn't recommend it for carpet (unless the dense hard stuff). The bright colors and ever present Mickey marketing seem to help keep the kids going as well.  As noted in another review, this isn't really interactive or educational, but it's a fine toy.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, Silly Wheelie Mickey

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player I looked forward to playing this game, but was very disappointed. It sounds fun - each player rolls five dice and adds their roll to the roll of a common die. I thought it would be more like Yahtzee, but it was not nearly as fun as that classic game. The common die gives the chance for each player to double their score, which helps someone come from behind and catch up with the player that is leading. However, when rolling only 5 dice, the odds of getting a decent roll were slim. It was almost impossible to get anything more than a three of a kind, and that was hard to do. This made the game more frustrating than fun. I've never played the original Farkle, and we had to make some house rules because many portions of the instructions were unclear, which added to my frustration. The instructions referred to online video directions being available, but I didn't think it was worth having to watch a video to learn to play what should have been a very simple dice game.

For those familiar with Farkle, the common die may add an interesting twist, but the bubble-popper and dice risers are unnecessary. The bubble-popper for the common die does not roll the die well and seems like it would break after a few uses. We took the die out and rolled it by hand. This was much easier and kept the game moving more quickly. (On a side note, when we removed the die from the bubble-popper, it looked dirty!) The dice risers are rickety and make the play of the game more confusing. Since you can't combine the numbers you get on individual rolls, it's necessary to keep track of what you got on each roll within a round. It was impossible to do this on the risers, so we just started putting the dice aside from each roll and not using the risers at all.

The dice themselves are sturdy, even though the white coloring started coming off the numbers after only a couple of uses. I like that there are four sets in different colors so each player can have their own color. However, the red and orange were too similar in color and it was hard to tell them apart.

Overall, I think the dice risers and bubble-popper are flimsy and just a gimmick to make more out of the game than there is. It's not an exciting game and became very boring when it became clear it was too hard to get a decent score from an individual roll.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

text_fidelity_a:
MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries Big & fast are the best ways to describe this RC racer!

At 1:10 scale, the unit ships with everything you need to run EXCEPT batteries for the RC transmitter. You will need to provide some AA batteries here. Also, make sure to charge your running batteries first.

Unfortunately, you will only get about 10-15 minutes of run time per charge. So having the 2 included battery packs is nice. Although, if you swap them out back-to-back, the one charging will not be ready to go before your second battery depletes. And charge time is roughly 4 hours EACH. So, you actually need A LOT of spare batteries if you want to run your car without any downtime.

Outside of this concern, the car is a lot like a hobby RC vehicle that you would assemble from scratch. But at a fraction of the cost. However, the parts are probably not hobby grade, but good enough for the intended audience of this vehicle.

In the mid-eighties, I was really into RC racing (A Tamiya Frog for those who remember), but even back then this was an expensive hobby (I was around 14, so everything was expensive!) as you always wanted to upgrade something - motor, servos, shocks, tires, etc... And I wasn't even running anywhere near top of the line stuff.

In contrast, this unit ships complete for right around $110.00. So, if you're just getting into the hobby (or re-entering), then this car will make a fun introduction/re-introduction without breaking the bank.

Lastly, this thing is FAST. It's rated right around 30-32MPH. That may seem slow when the only comparison you may have is driving in a car at that speed. However, seeing one of the RC cars rocket down the street at 30+ miles per hour will quickly alter your perspective!

Overall, this is a great out of the box setup that's a ton of fun for a kid, an adult or the kid in every adult!
text_fidelity_b: MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries

Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue I looked at different types water tables and sand tables and combos and finally decided on this one. Price was unbeatable (purchased during prime day and got a great deal). I based my finally decision on the following factors:

1) Feedback: based on the feedback this seemed to be the best product out there regarding hour long entertainment, durability, quality, and price
2) Quality: It comes with a cover lid that is fastened via cords on each side allowing it to stay put during storms and it is such a tight fit that it may not let any critters in to access the water or sand
3) It is a combo: meaning it allows for versatility. You can either fill both sides with sand or water, sand and water, or rice (as per feedback when moving it indoors to keep the mess at bay and allow indoor fun during the winter months)
4) It has two drain plugs (one each side) to allow the water and/or sand to drain easily
5) Easy clean up
6) Light enough to move
7) It came with the umbrella for the times the deck has no shade. This is great to allow a little protection from the sun
8) Value and price. If you would get a water table and sandbox separate from each other you would ultimately pay more unless you are lucky and get it used or hand me down or have time to build your own sand box.

Only down side I found so far: My 17 months old son has discovered how fun it is to transfer the sand from his sand side to the water side to make mud (Thank you hubby lol). Either way it can get messy and a bit more cumbersome to clean the water side after his fun. Suggestion: drain the water and let the sun dry out the side and grab the vacuum. Simple and quickest method.

Recommendation I like to pass one from a feedback I read on another sand table product: Add a bit of cinnamon to your play sand to deter critters (in case they find a way in with the cover). It works.
text_fidelity_b: Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue

Skull Party Game | Bluffing Game | Strategy Game | Fun Game for Game Night | Family Board Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 13+ | 3-6 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Space Cowboys I really loved this game. Will disclose, I've only played it once since I've got it, but it was very fun that one time.

It takes what I love from Liar's Dice, but gives it more suspense in my opinion. Liar's Dice can reach a point where for certain someone is losing a die, but in Skull, sometimes, it's just a challenge of what you pick up, and who you know for a fact has a skull on their mat. I love the suicide bluffs people pull with putting a skull down then bidding, and the whole bidding idea is really fun to me too.

The art is really pretty, though there are a few skulls I think that look more boring than others, all look good. The material is a hard cardboard with great texturing, feels like a coaster almost, I think it can be very durable, but getting them out of their original squares was a little bit of a challenge to not tear any. I also love how small the box is, you could carry this to any place you want rather easily. I almost am a little sad that it only has enough for 6 players, I could easily see this going further than 6 players, but playing with 6 players, it was very fun. I loved every second.

I rate this highly because I love the set, but I will admit, this game could be easily played with cards instead of this. Ravensburger Underwater Paradise 9000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 17807 - Handcrafted Tooling, Durable Blueboard, Every Piece Fits Together Perfectly I know Ravensburger Puzzles are expensive, but worth every penny as they are simply The Best. We have bought them before but never in this huge 9000 piece size. For those not familiar with Ravensburger Puzzles, they are made of the finest sturdy cardboard, hand cut in Germany with such a razor sharp cutter that they leave no cardboard dust and the pieces have an unbelievably tight fit. They have no competitors, as no one comes close to their hand workmanship, bold colors and quality.

The 9000 pieces in this puzzle come in 2 bags- each makes half the puzzle. This makes it so much easier to work on, as we bought 2 pieces of cardboard from our craft store- each a little over 3 feet by 2 feet, to assemble each half on. This half size easily fits on our kitchen table and can be moved easily as well when it's on the cardboard. Included with the 2 puzzle bags is a 3 foot poster of the puzzle to assist you in assembling the beautifully colored pieces. When we were finished with both halves, the full 6 foot 4 inch by 4 1/2 foot puzzle took our breath away! The bold, vivid colors on this large size of all the underwater life looks like a breathtaking work of art just waiting to brighten up a wall in your home.

We decided to put it up on a wall, right behind the children's aquarium- talk about stunning! The only thing we had to decide, is do we use glue to permanently seal it before hanging, or do we seal it tightly in plastic from our local art store, then hang it. The kids said they wanted it in plastic, as they may want to do the puzzle again someday- so it is sealed tightly in plastic against cardboard, framed and hung. If you want this permanently glued, as many people do, all you need to do is buy MasterPieces Puzzle Glue, or any other good puzzle glue and a brush. (I never use the cardboard glue applicators, as the brush is much better). One 5 ounce bottle will seal a 2000 piece puzzle, so you'll need 4 or 5 bottles. You can spread this glue on the front, back or both sides for a permanent bond. It dries clear, so you don't even see the glue.

This 9000 piece high quality Ravensburger Puzzle is worth every cent for the enjoyment of creating a bold, big, beautiful underwater work of art, but what you ultimately gain when you are finished is a gorgeous stunning large wall covering for a bare wall in your home, and that alone is worth the price of these high quality puzzles!

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"

We can only let him play with it for an hour a day with big breaks because him whimpering with joy and the songs playing soon drive us crazy!
